title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the neighbouring pages. X is a (real 2-dimensional) surface and x a point of X. S_x is the circle of tangent directions at x, i.e. the 'link' of x. A_x is the ordered set of closed arcs of S_x; points count as degenerate arcs. Gr(A_x) is the groupoid obtained from A_x by inverting all inclusions. Gr_0(A_x) is its full subcategory on the one-point subsets.

The previous page (83)-(84) gives a canonical equivalence Gr_0(A_x) ≃ Π_1(S_x). An arc A with endpoints a, b gives inclusion isomorphisms {a} → A ← {b}, hence an arrow a → b. This arrow goes to the homotopy class of the path along A. It follows (85) that a functor Ψ: Π_1(S_x) → G into any groupoid G is the same thing as a functor Ψ: A_x → G (86) that sends inclusions to isomorphisms.

On this page Grothendieck states when (85) is an equivalence. The conditions are:
- G is connected;
- G has π_1 ≅ Z;
- for two distinct points a, b of S_x, let A and B be the two complementary arcs with endpoints a, b. The zig-zag (86bis) {a} → A ← {b} → B ← {a} defines an automorphism of {a} in Gr(A_x), namely the loop once around the circle. The corresponding automorphism of Ψ({a}) must generate Aut_G(Ψ({a})).

This is the standard criterion for a functor out of a connected groupoid with π_1 = Z to be an equivalence. Essential surjectivity needs G connected; full faithfulness at one object needs Z → Aut to be an isomorphism.

The programme that follows is to build a functor (87) A_x → Revêt(D_x^*), into coverings of the germ of punctured disc at x, satisfying this generator condition. To do so it suffices (88) to give a functor from A_x to the category of 1-connected (simply connected) germs of spaces over the germ D_x^*. Composing with a functor (89) from such germs to Revêt(D_x^*) then does the job. That functor sends a simply connected germ U over D_x^* to the corresponding fibre functor or universal-covering object.

Concretely, an arc A of directions should go to the germ of the angular sector at x that it spans. A sector is simply connected and so serves as a 'base point' for coverings of the punctured neighbourhood. The next page makes this intrinsic. Arcs are identified with closed cones C in the tangent space T_x(X), other than {0} and the whole space. The sector germ in X is defined via local isomorphisms (T_x X, 0) ≃ (X, x) with identity differential. Independence of the chart is obtained by passing to filter bases of cones C' strictly containing C, i.e. with C' − {0} a neighbourhood of C − {0}.

In short, this is a combinatorial/sectorial model of the fundamental groupoid of the punctured disc at a point. Sectors in the tangent space play the role of base points, close to 'tangential base points'. It is presumably destined for the study of germs of coverings and of local monodromy at punctures within the Longue Marche programme.
errors: No mathematical error. The equivalence criterion is correct; it implicitly needs a ≠ b so that A and B are genuine complementary arcs, and the page states this.

Gr(A_x) is only implicitly the localization of the arc poset at all arrows. Reading (83) as an equivalence needs closed proper arcs only, never the whole circle; this is implicit here and assumed on the previous page.
Functor (89) is only sketched. Its well-definedness as a functor (choice of base points within a simply connected germ) is not checked on this page.

ideas.what: The poset of closed arcs of a circle, with inclusions inverted, models the fundamental groupoid Π_1(S^1). Functors out of it into groupoids are functors from Π_1.
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid as localization of a poset of contractible pieces (Čech/Alexandrov-type combinatorial model); van Kampen for groupoids
ideas.usually_credited_to: R. Brown (groupoid van Kampen, 1960s); McCord (1966) for finite poset models
ideas.where_published: Similar localization ideas appear in Pursuing Stacks; this specific use is unpublished as far as I know

ideas.what: Criterion: a functor Π_1(S^1) → G is an equivalence iff G is connected, has π_1 ≅ Z, and the loop {a} → A ← {b} → B ← {a} maps to a generator.

Angular sectors at x (arcs of tangent directions), viewed as simply connected germs over the punctured disc, are used as base points (fibre functors) for coverings of D_x^*. The construction is made intrinsic via cones in T_x X modulo local isomorphisms with identity differential (next page).
ideas.usually_credited_to: P. Deligne (1989, 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points'); Y. Ihara; sectors also in Stokes phenomena theory (Malgrange, Ramis)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses base points 'at infinity' for Teichmüller groupoids; the sectorial construction here is not in published texts as far as I know

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a topological notion of tangential/sectorial base point. Arcs of directions at a puncture become simply connected sector germs, and these define a groupoid of base points canonically equivalent to the fundamental groupoid of the punctured disc. Chart-independence uses cones in T_xX up to identity-tangent local isomorphisms. This anticipates, at least in spirit, Deligne's tangential base points.
missed.quote: Nous allons donc définir un foncteur (87) A_x → Revêt(D_x^*) ... il suffit de définir un foncteur (88) A_x → catégorie des germes 1-connexes d'espaces, au-dessus du germe D_x^*
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck, in the post-1981 Longue Marche continuation, built tangential base points from sectors as a groupoid. That matters for the history of tangential base points in anabelian geometry and Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory. The 'groupoid of sectors' formulation, rather than a single tangent vector, is a slightly different, more canonical packaging.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is elementary. The interest is historical: a careful, intrinsic sector-based construction of base points for local coverings at a puncture, close to tangential base points, in unpublished Longue Marche material. Grothendieck's general awareness of base points 'at infinity' is known from the Esquisse, so this is not startling.
transcription_corrections: Subscripts read as 'n' should be 'x' throughout: A_x, S_x, D_x^*, Gr_0(A_x) (the n's are artifacts of the handwritten x).
Line 3: 'G est connexe et à π_1 ≃ Z' (the struck word before 'connexe' is illegible).

Probable reading: 'pour un couple (a,b) de pts a,b distincts de S_x, définissant deux arcs A et B d'extrémités a,b, définissant l'automorphisme de a dans Gr_0(A_x) i.e. dans Gr(A_x), composé de (86bis)'.
'l'automorphisme correspondant de Ψ({a}) dans G soit un générateur de Aut_G(Ψ({a}))' rather than 'l'élément correspondant'.
(88): 'catégorie des germes 1-connexes d'espaces, au-dessus du germe D_x^*'.
